questions.question_text: When must a South Dakota broker associate obtain Errors and Omissions insurance?
distractors: Only after closing their first transaction
questions.explanation: Proof of coverage must be filed before an active license is issued, again on renewal, and again on reactivation (ARSD 20:69:15:02). Coverage comes through the commission's group plan or a certified independent policy.

questions.question_text: What are the current E&O insurance coverage limits in South Dakota?
questions.explanation: The minimum is $100,000 single-limit coverage per claim and a $500,000 annual aggregate per licensee (ARSD 20:69:15:03). The deductible may not exceed one percent of the single limit — $1,000 — with a like amount for defense and investigation.

questions.question_text: A broker associate allows their E&O policy to lapse without obtaining new coverage. What is the consequence?
questions.correct_answer: The license goes inactive until proof of coverage is filed
distractors: A $50 late fee applies until coverage is restored
No consequence if they are not actively selling
questions.explanation: The commission places the license on inactive status as of the date coverage terminates, and the licensee must surrender the license and identification card (ARSD 20:69:15:08.01). No licensed activity may resume until proof of insurance is filed.

questions.question_text: Which type of SD licensee is NOT required to carry E&O insurance?
questions.correct_answer: All active licensees must carry E&O insurance
distractors: Property managers with fewer than 10 units
Broker associates in their first year
questions.explanation: Every licensee on active status must carry coverage; only inactive licensees are excused (SDCL 36-21A-119). That takes in brokers, broker associates, property managers, auctioneers, and residential rental agents — there is no small-portfolio or first-year exception.

questions.question_text: The SDREC helps licensees obtain E&O coverage through what mechanism?
distractors: Mandatory coverage through the Recovery Fund
questions.explanation: The commission bids out a group policy open to every licensee that the insurer may not cancel (SDCL 36-21A-120). A licensee may instead certify independent coverage, and a responsible broker may certify $500,000/$1,000,000 covering all associated licensees.
